theater: 巴士拉以南鹽沼與兩河下游

battle.name: 津芝叛亂
battle.theater: 巴士拉以南鹽沼與兩河下游
battle.brief: 公元869年9月，阿里·伊本·穆罕默德在巴士拉南方的鹽沼煽動被奴役的津芝人起事，871年攻陷巴士拉，879年一度逼近巴格達，最終在穆赫塔拉被圍兩年半，883年城破，首級沿沼澤水道示眾。卡面的亞述長矛短柄長刃、鐵鏃套筒，正是九世紀兩河步兵矛的祖型。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 交戰的兩方性質極不對稱。朝廷一方是阿拔斯王朝的中央軍：由哈里發與攝政的哈里發特使調度，以薩馬拉與巴格達為基地的禁軍、波斯人與突斯人奴兵部隊為骨幹，再加巴士拉與瓦西特一帶穆哈拉比（al-Muhallabi）家族的地方武裝、巴士拉大族巴希拉（Bahila）部族的兵力，以及仍自居於哈里發統屬之下的哈瓦利吉派與阿里派分隊；阿曼與設拉子的藩王名義上向哈里發朝貢，實則自行其是，據塔巴里記載，阿曼的統治者與設拉子的首長曾向起義方面提供援助與庇護，這說明中央的權威在伊拉克南部只靠稅收與一紙軍令維持，邊境諸侯早已各自為政。起義一方沒有國家機器，也沒有可承認的君主：核心是巴士拉鹽沼與美索不達米亞沼澤中被奴役的津芝人（Zanj），即經印度洋奴隸貿易運入、而在阿拉伯文獻中被一概記作黑種人群體的東非與東印度出身者；他們被分置於鹽沼的勞動營中，替巴士拉富戶開闢鹽田、疏浚運鹽的水道。此外還有半解放的奴隸、城市小手工業者、巴士拉周邊的農民與貝都因人陸續加入。起義方的組織形態是鬆散的聯盟：一個領袖、幾支在沼澤中游動的武裝隊伍、一支水上船隊與若干被奪取的城鎮據點，靠劫掠奪得的武器、馬匹與糧食維持，沒有常備後方。兩方力量的對比因此極為特殊：朝廷有編制、有經費、有攻城器械，卻被財政危機、宮廷內鬥與其他戰線牽制；起義方既無編制亦無經費，卻有地形、熟悉水道的小艇與夜襲的機動性。
countriesEn: The two sides were of radically unequal character. On the court side stood the central army of the Abbasid Caliphate, dispatched by the caliph and by the caliph's regent, based on Samarra and Baghdad, built on the guard and on the Persian and Turkish slave regiments, and reinforced by the troops of the al-Muhallabi family of Basra and Wasit, by the men of the great southern tribe of Bahila, and by detachments drawn from among the Kharijites and the Alids who still acknowledged the caliph. The princes of Oman and Siraf owed nominal tribute to the caliph but governed themselves, and al-Tabari records that the ruler of Oman and the lord of Siraf gave the insurgents aid and shelter, which shows that the authority of the centre in southern Iraq rested on nothing more than tax receipts and a sheet of paper, and that its feudatories on the frontier had long been their own masters. On the rebel side there was no state, no bureaucracy and no acknowledged sovereign. Its core was the Zanj of the salt marshes south of Basra and of the Mesopotamian marshes: East Africans and East Indians brought in by the Indian Ocean slave trade and recorded in Arabic under a general name for black peoples, put into labour camps in the salt flats to open salt pans and to dig the waterways that carried salt away. To them were added half-freed slaves, small craftsmen, cultivators from the countryside round Basra and Bedouin households who joined as the months went by. The organisation of the insurgents was therefore a loose confederation of revolt: a single leader, a few armed bands moving through the marshes, a flotilla of boats and a handful of towns taken and held, kept alive on weapons, horses and grain taken by force, with no rear area behind it. The contrast between the two sides is therefore peculiar. The court had an establishment, a budget and siege engines, yet it was pinned down by insolvency, by quarrels inside the palace and by other fronts. The insurgents had neither establishment nor budget, but they had the ground, small boats that could thread the waterways, and the mobility to strike by night.
people: 核心人物是阿里·伊本·穆罕默德（Ali ibn Muhammad），後人稱他為「津芝之首」（Sāhib al-Zanj）。他的出身在史料中互相矛盾：塔巴里記他為阿里·伊本·穆罕默德·伊本·阿卜杜·拉希姆，祖父拉希姆出自阿卜杜·蓋斯部族、生於波斯塔利坎，母系則為胡宰瑪的班·阿薩德；今人蓋恩·坎貝爾與菲利普·格蘭特多認為，他其實是生於雷伊一帶的波斯化阿拉伯人。861年薩馬拉陷入「薩馬拉無政府狀態」，他先混跡於穆塔西爾宮中有影響力的奴僕之間，863年跑到東阿拉伯的巴林（Bahrayn）假裝什葉派起事，失敗後於868年轉入巴士拉，試圖利用巴士拉城內比拉利派與薩德派兩大派系的衝突，失敗被擒，解送瓦西特後很快脫身，又在巴格達停留一年，假冒栽德派後裔、宣稱自己是先知後人，以招攬人望。869年他回到巴士拉，開始在鹽沼的奴役營中逐個探問黑奴的處境與口糧，承諾財富與飽暖以換取支持，隨即自居領袖，用哈瓦利吉派「除了真主別無仲裁」的口號書寫旗幟與錢幣，卻又保留阿里派的說法。他的部將分工明確：葉海亞·伊本·穆罕默德·巴赫拉尼、阿里·伊本·阿萬·穆哈拉比、蘇萊曼·伊本·賈米、蘇萊曼·伊本·穆薩·沙爾拉尼分別在沼澤各處作戰，兒子安卡萊在最後的攻守中擔任要角。朝廷方面，實際掌權的是攝政的穆瓦法克（阿布·艾哈邁德·伊本·穆塔維克），他在872年的反擊中吃了敗仗，直到879年底才重新部署，880年親率大軍進軍，881年2月圍困穆赫塔拉，以「凡降者免罪」的招撫代替強攻；其子阿布·阿巴斯（後來的穆塔迪德哈里發）自880年起即以主力身份出征，883年11月30日入巴格達舉行凱旋式。將領方面還有穆薩·伊本·布加、阿布·阿爾·薩吉（景教徒將軍）、馬斯魯爾·巴爾希、艾哈邁德·伊本·萊斯塔韋、易卜拉欣·伊本·穆罕默德等，都是哈里發麾下指揮大型兵團的名字。
peopleEn: The man at the centre was Ali ibn Muhammad, called by later writers Sahib al-Zanj, the Chief of the Zanj. His origins are contradictory in the sources: al-Tabari gives him as Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim, with a grandfather of the Arab tribe Abd al-Qays born at al-Taliqan and a mother of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah; modern scholars such as Gwyn Campbell and Philip Grant hold that he was in fact an Arab of Persian origin from the neighbourhood of Rayy. When Samarra fell into the Anarchy at Samarra in 861, he mixed with influential slaves of the palace of al-Muntasir; in 863 he went to Bahrayn in eastern Arabia, posed as a Shi'ite and stirred up a rising, and after it collapsed he moved to Basra in 868, where he tried to exploit the quarrel between the rival Bilaliyyah and Sa'diyyah factions of the city, was arrested and carried to Wasit, escaped quickly, and spent a year in Baghdad, where he claimed kinship with the descendants of Zayd ibn Ali and passed himself off as a Zaydi in order to win adherents. In 869 he returned to the region of Basra and began to go among the black slaves of the marshes, asking after their conditions and their rations, promising wealth and full measure in return for their support, and he soon took for himself the name of leader, wrote the Kharijite formula that there is no arbitration except by God upon his banners and his coins, and at the same time kept up the pretence of the Alids. His commanders had their own spheres of action: Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Bahrani, Ali ibn Aban al-Muhallabi, Sulayman ibn Jami' and Sulayman ibn Musa al-Sha'rani each fought in different parts of the marshes, and his son Ankalay played a leading part in the last campaigns. On the court side the effective ruler was the regent al-Muwaffaq, Abu Ahmad ibn al-Mutawakkil, whose counter-stroke of 872 ended in failure and who did not redeploy until late 879, joining the campaign in person in 880 and investing al-Mukhtarah in February 881, using amnesty rather than assault. His son Abu al-'Abbas, the future caliph al-Mu'tadid, led a main force from 880 onwards and entered Baghdad in triumph on 30 November 883. Among the commanders stand also Musa ibn Bugha, Abu al-Saj Devdad, a Nestorian general, Masrur al-Balkhi, Ahmad ibn Laythawayh and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, all names that led large field armies under the caliph.
kits: 卡面上的亞述長矛是公元前九世紀新亞述王朝的制式步兵矛：短柄、長刃，鐵矛頭以套筒固定在木杆前端，與弓並列在亞述步兵的配裝之中，兩河流域的城一個接一個在這樣的矛尖前陷落。它並沒有出現在九世紀的伊拉克戰場上；中世紀伊斯蘭世界的長矛，無論阿拉伯部族的標槍、波斯系的塞矛，還是禁軍的步兵矛，都是鐵矛頭配木杆的直刺兵器，形制上正是亞述矛的後裔：短柄便於在沼澤、舟船與窄巷之間揮動，長而窄的刃口適合刺穿軟甲與皮甲而不是橫劈，起義的津芝步兵靠的正是這類短柄鐵矛。卡面兵器標記的是這一條技術譜系，而不是一件出土的實物。實際的配裝大致如下：起義軍的戰鬥人員以步兵為主，配短柄鐵矛、投矛、柳葉形單刃刀、斧（沼澤伐木與砍柵之用）與弓；防護極簡，多數人只有一面小圓盾（皮或木）或以衣物裹身，這與他們在勞動營中根本沒有能力取得裝備的處境一致。他們的弓是復合反曲弓，箭鏃多為骨或鐵。起義方還自造了舟隊，得以在鹽沼的運鹽水道、盲底格里斯河與通往巴士拉的運河上快速轉進，船上以矛、弓與火為主，專打官方水路上的巡邏與運糧船隊，這是他們十四年不滅的關鍵。官軍方面，步兵仍以矛、彎刀（阿拉伯式新月劍）與弓弩為主，弩的數量有限；騎兵是哈里發軍的骨幹，以突斯人與波斯人奴兵充當，配長矛、刀、弓箭與鎖子甲、鱗甲；攻城則有撞木、弩機、投石與火油，圍城時靠壕壘與封鎖水道把守軍困在城內。交通方面，底格里斯河與運河是整場戰爭的走廊，官方以駁船運兵運糧，起義方則用自造的小艇與蘆葦編的船。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is the standard infantry spear of the Neo-Assyrian Empire of the ninth century BC: a short haft, a long blade, an iron head socketed onto the front of the wooden shaft, carried together with the bow in the equipment of the Assyrian infantry, before which the cities of Mesopotamia fell one after another. It did not itself appear on a battlefield in Iraq in the ninth century. The spears of the medieval Islamic world, whether the lance of the Arab tribes, the saagh of the Persians or the infantry spear of the guard, were thrusting weapons of an iron head on a wooden shaft, and in form they were the descendants of the Assyrian spear: the short haft was convenient to wield in marshes, in boats and in narrow lanes, and the long narrow blade was fitted to pierce soft and leather armour rather than to slash. The Zanj footmen fought with exactly such short-hafted iron spears. What the card marks is this line of technical descent, not an excavated object. The actual equipment was roughly as follows. The fighting men of the insurgents were for the most part infantry, equipped with short-hafted iron spears, javelins, single-edged willow-leaf blades, axes used in cutting timber and palisades in the marshes, and bows; protection was minimal, most men having only a small round shield of leather or wood or wrapping themselves in their clothing, which agrees with the fact that in the labour camps they had no means of obtaining equipment at all. Their bows were composite recurved bows, the arrowheads of bone or iron. The insurgents also built their own flotilla, which let them move quickly along the salt canals, the Blind Tigris and the waterways leading to Basra, their boats armed with spears, bows and fire, and they struck at the patrols and the grain fleets of the government on the rivers; that was the key to their survival for fourteen years. On the government side the infantry still carried the spear, the curved sword of the Arab pattern and the bow, with crossbows present but scarce; the cavalry was the backbone of the caliph's army, filled out with Turkish and Persian slave soldiers, equipped with long spears, swords, bows and coats of mail and scale armour; for sieges there were battering beams, crossbow mechanisms, stone-throwers and fire oil, and in a blockade the defenders were shut in by trenches and by the closing of the waterways. In transport, the Tigris and the canals formed the corridor of the whole war, the state moving men and grain on lighters, while the insurgents used their own small boats and reed-built craft.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術可以歸納為一句話：以沼澤與水道為依托的游擊與襲擾，最後再以攻城定生死。開戰初期，阿里·伊本·穆罕默德並沒有正面攻打巴士拉，而是退入沼澤：白天潛藏，夜晚襲擊城鎮、莊園與官軍營壘，奪取武器、馬匹、糧食與俘虜，釋放同族奴隸，縱火燒掉其餘物資以延緩官軍報復；同時在沼澤中築壘、修造船隊、控制運河，在所據之地徵收土地稅並自行鑄造帶哈瓦利吉派字樣的錢幣，形成一個能夠自給的小型政權。攻擊城鎮採多路夜襲、突然出現於敵前、得手即撤的方式，絕不糾纏：870年攻下巴士拉以北的烏布拉，871年奪取胡茲斯坦方向的蘇克·阿赫瓦茲，同年9月在長期圍困之後攻陷巴士拉城。兵鋒的極限出現在879年，起義軍攻破瓦西特與拉姆胡爾木茲，沿底格里斯河北上，一度逼近巴格達約五十英里（約八十公里），令中央震動。防守上，起義方依賴沼澤水道與以蘆葦築成的沼澤民居式堡壘，官軍的騎兵在鹽沼中難以展開，官軍的水上船隊反而常在窄水道中被襲。官軍的戰術則相反：一是分割包圍、以河渠封鎖切斷鹽沼裏的糧水；二是圍而不急攻、配合招撫。879年底穆瓦法克先遣其子阿布·阿巴斯率主力掃清伊拉克與阿哈瓦茲兩個戰區，把起義軍逼回巴士拉以南的穆赫塔拉；880年穆瓦法克本人率大軍會師，881年2月開始圍城，長達兩年半，最終在883年8月破城，叛軍首領在逃亡中被殺或被擒，朝廷奪回沼澤之後，又以舟船沿水道展示其首級。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the insurgents can be put in one phrase: harassment and raid based on the marshes and the waterways, and at the last a siege to decide everything. In the opening phase Ali ibn Muhammad did not attack Basra frontally but withdrew into the marshes: by day he lay hidden, by night he struck at towns, estates and government camps, taking weapons, horses, food and prisoners, freeing slaves of his own kind and burning the rest to delay the government's revenge. At the same time he built strongholds in the marshes, made a flotilla, controlled the canals, levied land tax in the territory he held and minted his own coins with Kharijite inscriptions upon them, forming a small polity able to feed itself. Attacks on towns were carried out by night in several columns, appearing suddenly in front of the enemy and withdrawing as soon as the work was done, and never allowing themselves to be drawn into a set-piece engagement. Al-Ubulla north of Basra fell in 870, Suq al-Ahwaz in the direction of Khuzestan was taken in 871, and in September of that same year the city of Basra fell after a long blockade. The limit of their advance came in 879, when they carried Wasit and Ramhurmuz, moved north-west along the Tigris and came within about fifty miles, some eighty kilometres, of Baghdad, shaking the centre. On the defensive they relied on the marsh waterways and on strongholds built of reeds in the fashion of the marsh dwellings, where the cavalry of the government could not deploy and where the government flotillas were repeatedly attacked in narrow channels. The tactics of the government were the opposite: first, to encircle in separate groups and cut off food and water in the salt marshes by closing the rivers and canals; second, to invest without pressing the assault and to work on the population through offers of pardon. At the end of 879 al-Muwaffaq sent his son Abu al-'Abbas with a main force to clear the two theatres of Iraq and al-Ahwaz and to drive the insurgents back to al-Mukhtarah south of Basra; in 880 al-Muwaffaq himself joined with a great army; in February 881 the siege of al-Mukhtarah began and lasted two and a half years, ending with the fall of the city in August 883, the rebel leader killed or taken in his flight, and the government, once it had recovered the marshes, carrying his head on a boat along the waterways.
data: 這場戰爭的數字要分成可核與不可核兩類。可核的首先是系年：起事繫於公元869年9月，871年9月巴士拉陷落，876年起義軍控制巴士拉與瓦西特之間的沼澤，879年戰線北推到瓦西特與拉姆胡爾木茲一線並逼近巴格達約五十英里，879年底朝廷重新發動大規模進攻，880年穆瓦法克親至，881年2月穆赫塔拉被圍，883年8月城破，883年11月30日阿布·阿巴斯入巴格達凱旋，合計十四年。可核的第二類是距離與地理：巴士拉至巴格達直線約四百五十公里，沿底格里斯河航道順流而下約需十餘日；巴士拉以南的穆赫塔拉在鹽沼深處，離城約五六十公里，路上盡是鹽田與運鹽水道，夏季地面鹽殼硬化尚可行軍，春秋水漲時沼澤大部分沒入水中，隊伍只能乘舟；胡茲斯坦的阿哈瓦茲戰區在底格里斯與卡倫兩河之間，與巴士拉之間靠運河相連。不可核的是兵數：起義軍在高峰期被記述為數萬之眾，官軍遠征軍的規模同樣以數萬計，但雙方的點名數只在零星戰鬥裏留下幾百至數千人級別的記載（例如守軍出城反擊時的損失），全國總兵力與佔領區的稅收規模都無從核實。關於全役的總損失，史料所給數字互相矛盾，量級由數十萬至數百萬不等，現代史家普遍視為誇張；塔巴里只逐戰記錄，較為可用。唯一可以確定的是：朝廷為此投入的兵員與軍費已近它當年財政能動用的極限——薩馬拉無政府狀態期間的欠餉、兵變與865至866年的內戰，已把中央推到破產邊緣。
dataEn: The numbers of this war fall into two classes, the verifiable and the unverifiable. The verifiable are, first, the chronology. The rising is tied to September 869; Basra fell in September 871; in 876 the insurgents held the marshes between Basra and Wasit; in 879 the front was pushed north to the line of Wasit and Ramhurmuz and came to within some fifty miles of Baghdad; at the end of 879 the government launched a major offensive again; al-Muwaffaq came in person in 880; al-Mukhtarah was invested in February 881; the city fell in August 883; and on 30 November 883 Abu al-'Abbas entered Baghdad in triumph. Fourteen years in all. The second verifiable class is distance and geography. The straight line from Basra to Baghdad is about four hundred and fifty kilometres, and the run down the Tigris took something over ten days; al-Mukhtarah lies deep in the salt marshes south of Basra, some fifty to sixty kilometres from the city, the road running through salt pans and salt canals, with the crust of the ground hardened in summer so that troops could march, while in spring and autumn the floods put most of the marsh under water and the columns could travel only by boat; the theatre of al-Ahwaz in Khuzestan lies between the Tigris and the Karkh and is joined to Basra by canal. What cannot be verified are the numbers of men. The insurgents are described at their height as tens of thousands, and the size of the government expeditionary army is likewise put in the tens of thousands, but the enumerated figures survive only for a few engagements, where the losses of a sallying garrison are given in the hundreds or the thousands; the total strength of either side and the scale of the revenue of the occupied districts cannot be checked. On the total losses of the war the sources contradict one another, the magnitudes running from the hundreds of thousands to the millions, and modern historians treat them generally as gross exaggerations; al-Tabari, who records battle by battle, is the more usable witness. One thing can be certain: the men and the money the court committed to this were close to the limit of what its finances could move, for the arrears of pay, the mutinies and the civil war of 865 to 866 in the Anarchy at Samarra had already brought the centre to the edge of bankruptcy.
cause: 起義的成因有四層，彼此咬合。第一層是經濟與制度：巴士拉港的富戶在薩瓦德地區佔有大量鹽沼荒地，這些地因農民外流與反覆水淹而一度廢棄，要把它們恢復成可耕地與鹽場，就必須靠密集的奴役勞動；大量東非與東印度出身的奴隸被運入，置於鹽沼的勞動營中，剝去表層含氮的土、疏浚運鹽的水道，條件極為惡劣，管理嚴酷而供給不足，西曆六八九至六九〇年與六九四年已有兩次同類反抗，都很快被平定，此後文獻沉默了兩百年。第二層是中央的崩解：861年起薩馬拉陷入無政府狀態，哈里發與禁軍爭權，十年間六位哈里發先後即位，欠餉引發兵變，865至866年內戰，866年哈瓦利吉派大亂，國家近乎破產；伊拉克南部的總督可以自行其是，邊境藩王不再聽命，中央既無力賑濟鹽沼的勞動營，也無力在稅收銳減之際養兵。第三層是本地矛盾的激化：巴士拉城內比拉利派與薩德派爭鬥不休，雙方都以武力解決；城外鹽沼的居民則在莊園經營與人身依附之間被榨乾。第四層是號召的策略：阿里·伊本·穆罕默德審時度勢，選用哈瓦利吉派「最有資格者當統治，哪怕他是阿比西尼亞奴隸」的主張作為旗幟，把一場經濟上的反抗翻譯成一個正統的宗教與政治的命題，並以同一句「除了真主別無仲裁」的口號貫穿旗幟、錢幣與佈道，於是奴隸、農人、城市貧民、手工業者與不滿的部族在同一面旗下聚合。
causeEn: The causes of the rising run in four layers, each locked into the next. The first is economic and institutional. Wealthy households of the port of Basra held large tracts of the salt marshes of the Sawad, land that had fallen out of cultivation through the flight of the peasants and repeated flooding, and to bring it back under the plough and the salt pans meant dense servile labour. Large numbers of slaves from East Africa and East India were brought in and set up in labour camps in the marshes to strip the nitrogenous topsoil and to dredge the salt channels; the conditions were appalling, the management harsh and the rations poor. Two earlier risings of the same kind, in 689 to 690 and in 694, had been crushed quickly, and after that the literature is silent for two centuries. The second layer is the collapse of the centre. From 861 Samarra was in the Anarchy at Samarra, with the caliph and the military establishment fighting for the state; six caliphs succeeded one another in ten years, arrears of pay brought mutinies, there was civil war in 865 and 866 and a great rising of the Kharijites in 866, and the state was near bankruptcy. Governors of southern Iraq were left to act on their own, the feudatories of the frontier no longer obeyed, and the centre could neither feed the labour camps of the marshes nor maintain an army on revenues that were shrinking. The third layer is the sharpening of local conflict. Inside Basra the Bilaliyyah and Sa'diyyah factions fought each other with arms, and outside the city the inhabitants of the marshes were squeezed between the management of the estates and their own personal bondage. The fourth layer is the strategy of the appeal. Ali ibn Muhammad judged his moment and took up the Kharijite claim that the most qualified man should rule even if he were an Abyssinian slave, turning an economic rebellion into an orthodox religious and political proposition, and he ran the same formula, that there is no arbitration except by God, through his banners, his coins and his sermons, so that slaves, peasants, the poor of the towns, craftsmen and discontented tribes gathered under one flag.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果分近遠兩層。近的一層是戰區的破壞：巴士拉與周邊城鎮反覆易手，鹽田與運河系統屢遭摧毀，阿哈瓦茲與伊拉克南部的水利交通在十四年裡幾乎停擺，底格里斯河上的商旅與糧運時斷時續，鹽業與糧食供應長期失衡；起義軍所鑄的錢幣與哈瓦利吉派口號一度在市面流通，說明政府對這一區的貨幣與稅收控制一度中斷。遠的一層是政治格局的重排：朝廷把大批兵員、經費與注意力釘在伊拉克南部十四年，埃及的圖倫王朝總督艾哈邁德·伊本·圖倫趁勢取得實質獨立，建立起可延續三十餘年的政權；薩法里王朝的雅庫布·伊本·萊斯與其兄弟阿姆魯在東方各省站穩腳跟，876年雅庫布甚至率軍西向伊戰克，而中央竟無力有效阻止；東線對拜占庭的防禦也因兵力分散而出現漏洞，巴林地區的伊斯蘭主義運動則可能在這段空窗期內坐大。學術影響同樣可觀：《津芝紀事》（Akhbar al-Zanj，一般認為出自一位曾在起義軍中任職、後來改宗的景教徒之手）與塔巴里的《聖徒與諸王史》構成本場戰爭最核心的兩份材料，諾爾德克、馬西尼翁以及後來的波波維奇等人依據這些材料重構了事件過程；而關於「津芝」究竟指東非海岸的黑人、泛指非洲人，還是包含大量波斯與阿拉伯裔自由民的集合，學界至今仍在爭論。這場戰爭之所以重要，正因為它同時是一次大規模奴隸起義、一次帶有哈瓦利吉派式平等訴求的政治運動、一次伊斯蘭世界有完整記載的水上游擊戰，也是一個關於奴隸制在阿拔斯經濟中究竟佔有什麼位置的長期案例。
impactEn: The consequences of the war fall into an immediate and a distant layer. The immediate layer is the damage done to the theatre. Basra and the towns around it changed hands again and again, the salt pans and the canal system were repeatedly wrecked, the waterworks and the traffic of southern Iraq and al-Ahwaz were all but stopped for the fourteen years, the caravans and the grain traffic on the Tigris were interrupted again and again, and the supply of salt and of food was thrown out of balance for a long time; the coins struck by the insurgents and the Kharijite formulae on them circulated for a while, which shows that the control of money and of taxation in that district broke down for a time. The distant layer is the rearrangement of the political map. With large numbers of men, much money and all its attention pinned to southern Iraq for fourteen years, Ahmad ibn Tulun, governor of Egypt for the Tulunids, took advantage to win effective independence and to establish a regime that was to outlive him by more than three decades; Ya'qub ibn al-Layth of the Saffarids and his brother Amr established themselves in the eastern provinces, and in 876 Ya'qub even marched west into Iraq without meeting effective opposition from the centre; the defence of the eastern frontier against Byzantium showed gaps through the dispersal of the armies, and the Islamic movement in Bahrain may have grown large in that same window. The scholarly effect is no less real. The Akhbar al-Zanj, generally attributed to a Nestorian convert who had once served in the insurgents' camp, and al-Tabari's History of the Prophets and Kings are the two principal sources for the whole affair, and on them Theodor Nöldeke, Louis Massignon and, later, Alexandre Popović rebuilt the course of events; whether the Zanj meant the blacks of the East African coast, Africans in general, or a collectivity that included a great many free Persians and Arabs is still debated. The war matters precisely because it was at once a mass rising of slaves, a political movement carrying a Kharijite kind of claim to equality, the best-documented riverine guerrilla war in the Islamic world, and a long-running case study of what slavery actually meant in the Abbasid economy.
result: 結局是朝廷的勝利與起義軍的徹底崩潰。879年底起，穆瓦法克把兵力集中到伊拉克與阿哈瓦茲兩個戰區，先以主力掃清沿底格里斯河北岸的據點，把起義軍擠回巴士拉以南的穆赫塔拉；880年他親率大軍會師，在鹽沼中步步為營，切斷水道、封死陸路；881年2月起對穆赫塔拉圍城，整整圍了兩年半。這期間朝廷沒有一味強攻，而是配合招撫——凡投降者免罪、既往不咎，據塔巴里記載，許多人因此離開起義軍回到政府一方，起義軍的兵力與士氣在圍城之中被慢慢耗盡。883年8月穆赫塔拉城破，阿里·伊本·穆罕默德在逃亡中被殺或被擒，他與主要部將的頭顱被懸在矛尖上，再以船隻沿運河與沼澤水道往來展示，宣告領袖已死；餘部或降或散，鹽沼重回朝廷統治。883年11月30日，穆瓦法克之子、未來的哈里發穆塔迪德率軍進入巴格達，舉行凱旋式，再次展示阿里·伊本·穆罕默德的首級。十四年之後，伊拉克南部的秩序表面上回復了：鹽田與運河重新整理，鹽稅與關稅恢復徵收，舊日的奴役營被拆散，餘下的奴隸或被遣返原籍、或被轉賣。然而代價是顯而易見的：朝廷耗盡了對薩馬拉亂局本就捉襟見肘的財政，丟失了數個省的實際控制，讓東方的薩法里王朝與西面的埃及自治勢力各自坐大；河運與鹽業的復原用了數十年，而被這場戰爭牽動的奴隸制與哈瓦利吉派理想，在往後的巴林、波斯與北非留下了長遠的回響。
resultEn: The end was a victory for the court and the total collapse of the insurgents. From the end of 879 al-Muwaffaq concentrated his strength in the two theatres of Iraq and al-Ahwaz, cleared the strongholds along the north bank of the Tigris with his main force and squeezed the insurgents back into al-Mukhtarah south of Basra; in 880 he joined with a great army in person and advanced by measured steps through the salt marshes, cutting the waterways and closing the land routes; from February 881 he invested al-Mukhtarah, and the siege ran for two and a half years. Throughout, the court did not simply batter. It worked on the population: those who came in were pardoned and their pasts let go, and al-Tabari records that many men left the insurgents in consequence, so that the strength and the heart of the rebels were worn away little by little inside the blockade. In August 883 the city of al-Mukhtarah fell; Ali ibn Muhammad was killed or taken in his flight, and his head and those of his chief commanders were mounted on lance points and then carried on boats along the canals and the marsh waterways, to make it known that the leader was dead; the rest either surrendered or scattered, and the salt marshes returned to the government. On 30 November 883 al-Muwaffaq's son, the future caliph al-Mu'tadid, entered Baghdad in triumph and once more displayed the head of Ali ibn Muhammad. Fourteen years on, order in southern Iraq had been restored on the surface: the salt pans and canals were put in order again, the salt tax and the customs were resumed, the old labour camps were broken up, and the slaves who remained were either sent back to their homes or sold on. The cost, however, is plain. The court exhausted a treasury that the anarchy at Samarra had already left threadbare, it lost effective control of several provinces, and it let the Saffarids in the east and the autonomous authorities in Egypt grow strong in their own directions; the recovery of the river traffic and of the salt trade took decades; and the questions of slavery and of Kharijite equality that the war had set moving left a long echo in Bahrain, in Persia and in North Africa afterwards.
